AIT should be considered as a preventive strategy in allergic diseases
nodes.content: Given its potential to modify immune responses and reduce the risk of disease progression, AIT should be considered as a preventive strategy in the management of allergic diseases.

nodes.name: AIT is effective for allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, and venom allergy.
nodes.content: AIT has demonstrated clinical efficacy in reducing symptoms and medication needs for allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, and moderate to severe venom allergy. It is considered a reliable therapeutic option for these conditions.

nodes.name: AIT should be considered as a preventive strategy in allergic disease management.
nodes.content: AIT has the potential to induce immunological changes that result in immune modification, making it a viable preventive strategy for allergic diseases. This includes preventing the development of new sensitizations or allergic conditions in at-risk individuals.

nodes.name: There is a need for more high-quality clinical trials on AIT's preventive potential.
nodes.content: Although evidence exists for AIT as a disease-modifying treatment with preventive potential, there is an urgent need for more robust clinical trials to better understand its efficacy in preventing allergic sensitization, first allergic diseases, and allergic comorbidities.

nodes.name: AIT induces immunological changes that may lead to immune modification.
nodes.content: AIT has the potential to induce immunological changes that result in immune system modification. This supports its role as a preventive strategy in allergic diseases.

nodes.name: AIT is effective for allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, and venom allergy
nodes.content: AIT has demonstrated clinical efficacy for allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, and moderate to severe venom allergy. It leads to sustained symptom reduction and decreased need for symptomatic treatment.

nodes.name: AIT may have long-term preventive effects on asthma symptoms and medication needs
nodes.content: Some trial data suggest that the preventive effects of AIT on asthma symptoms and medication needs may extend beyond two years post-treatment. However, more evidence is needed to confirm these long-term benefits.

nodes.name: AIT can prevent asthma in children and adolescents with allergic rhinitis (AR).
nodes.content: A three-year course of subcutaneous or sublingual AIT is recommended for children and adolescents with moderate to severe AR triggered by grass or birch pollen. This treatment can prevent asthma for up to two years post-AIT and has sustained effects on AR symptoms and medication use.

nodes.name: A three-year course of AIT is recommended for children and adolescents with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis
nodes.content: The guideline recommends a three-year course of subcutaneous or sublingual AIT for children and adolescents with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis triggered by grass or birch pollen. This treatment can prevent asthma for up to two years post-AIT and sustain the reduction of AR symptoms and medication needs.

nodes.name: Evidence for AIT's preventive effects on allergic sensitization and other allergens is limited
nodes.content: There is insufficient evidence to confirm the preventive effects of AIT for allergic sensitization or for allergic rhinitis triggered by house dust mites or other allergens. More high-quality clinical trials are needed to establish its efficacy in these areas.

nodes.name: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a disease-modifying treatment for IgE-mediated allergic diseases.
nodes.content: AIT has been shown to provide therapeutic benefits beyond cessation of treatment, with potential preventive effects against the development of new allergic conditions. It is particularly effective in reducing symptoms and medication requirements for allergic rhinitis (AR), allergic asthma, and venom allergy.

nodes.name: Children with allergic rhinitis are at higher risk of developing asthma
nodes.content: Children with allergic rhinitis have a threefold increased risk of developing asthma. This highlights the importance of preventive strategies, such as AIT, to reduce the progression of allergic diseases.

nodes.name: Evidence for AIT's preventive effects on house dust mite-triggered AR and other allergens is limited
nodes.content: While AIT shows promise in preventing asthma in children with AR triggered by grass or birch pollen, there is insufficient evidence regarding its preventive effects in individuals with AR caused by house dust mites or other allergens. Further research is required in these areas.

nodes.name: AIT has potential preventive effects on allergic sensitization and co-morbidities.
nodes.content: AIT may help prevent the development of allergic sensitization, the first allergic disease, or allergic co-morbidities in individuals with existing allergic conditions. However, more high-quality clinical trials are needed to confirm these effects.

nodes.name: AIT should be considered as a preventive strategy for allergic diseases
nodes.content: Given its potential to induce immune modification and reduce the risk of developing asthma in children with allergic rhinitis, AIT is recommended as a preventive strategy for managing allergic diseases. This approach could help mitigate the long-term burden of these conditions.

nodes.name: AIT can prevent asthma in children and adolescents with allergic rhinitis triggered by grass or birch pollen.
nodes.content: A three-year course of subcutaneous or sublingual AIT is recommended for children and adolescents with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis caused by grass or birch pollen. This treatment can prevent asthma for up to two years post-AIT and has sustained effects on allergic rhinitis symptoms.

nodes.name: AIT has potential for preventing allergic sensitization and allergic comorbidities
nodes.content: AIT may prevent the development of allergic sensitization, the first allergic disease, or allergic comorbidities in individuals with existing allergic conditions. However, there is an urgent need for more high-quality clinical trials to substantiate these preventive effects.

nodes.name: More evidence is needed for AIT in preventing allergic diseases triggered by house dust mites.
nodes.content: While AIT shows promise in preventing allergic diseases, its efficacy for allergic rhinitis triggered by house dust mites or other allergens remains less clear. Further research is required to establish its preventive potential in these cases.

nodes.name: AIT shows potential for long-term prevention of asthma symptoms.
nodes.content: Some trial data suggest that the preventive effects of AIT on asthma symptoms and medication use may extend beyond two years after the completion of therapy. However, more evidence is needed to confirm these long-term benefits.

nodes.name: Evidence for AIT's preventive effects on house dust mite-triggered AR and other allergens is limited.
nodes.content: While AIT has shown promise in preventing asthma in cases of AR triggered by grass or birch pollen, there is insufficient evidence regarding its preventive efficacy for AR triggered by house dust mites or other allergens. Further research is necessary in these areas.

nodes.name: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a disease-modifying treatment for IgE-mediated allergic diseases.
nodes.content: AIT has been demonstrated to provide therapeutic benefits beyond its cessation and has the potential for preventive effects. It is effective in reducing symptoms and medication needs for allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, and venom allergies.

nodes.name: AIT induces immunological changes that may modify immune responses
nodes.content: AIT has the potential to induce immunological changes, leading to immune modification. This mechanism supports its role as a preventive strategy in allergic diseases.

nodes.name: AIT may have long-term preventive effects on asthma symptoms and medication use.
nodes.content: Some trial data suggest that AIT can have a preventive effect on asthma symptoms and medication use beyond two years after treatment. However, more evidence is needed to confirm these long-term effects.

nodes.name: Children with allergic rhinitis have a higher risk of developing asthma.
nodes.content: Children diagnosed with allergic rhinitis are three times more likely to develop asthma compared to those without allergic rhinitis. This highlights the importance of preventive strategies like AIT in this population.

nodes.name: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a disease-modifying treatment with preventive potential
nodes.content: AIT is recognized as a treatment that not only reduces symptoms and medication needs for IgE-mediated allergic diseases but also has the potential to prevent the development of new allergic conditions. This preventive effect may extend beyond the cessation of AIT, particularly in children with allergic rhinitis (AR), reducing their risk of developing asthma.

nodes.name: More evidence is needed for AIT's preventive effects on allergic sensitization and other allergic conditions.
nodes.content: While AIT shows promise as a preventive strategy, there is insufficient evidence for its effectiveness in preventing allergic sensitization, the first allergic disease, or allergic comorbidities in individuals with other allergic conditions. High-quality clinical trials are urgently needed.

nodes.name: Allergic diseases impose a significant burden on individuals and society
nodes.content: Allergic diseases, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, and allergic rhinitis, are common chronic conditions that often begin in childhood and persist into adulthood. They significantly impact quality of life, healthcare costs, and economic productivity due to work and school absences.

nodes.name: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a disease-modifying treatment for IgE-mediated allergic diseases
nodes.content: AIT has demonstrated both therapeutic effects and potential preventive effects in IgE-mediated allergic diseases. It can reduce symptoms and medication needs, and may prevent the development of new allergic conditions, such as asthma in children with allergic rhinitis.

nodes.name: Children with allergic rhinitis are at increased risk of developing asthma.
nodes.content: Research indicates that children with allergic rhinitis have a threefold higher risk of developing asthma. This highlights the importance of early intervention and preventive strategies such as AIT.

nodes.name: AIT may reduce the risk of developing asthma in children with allergic rhinitis.
nodes.content: Studies indicate that children with AR are at a three-fold increased risk of developing asthma. AIT has been shown to potentially reduce this risk by inducing immunological changes that modify the immune response.

nodes.name: AIT can prevent asthma development in children with allergic rhinitis.
nodes.content: A three-year course of subcutaneous or sublingual AIT for children and adolescents with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis triggered by grass or birch pollen can prevent asthma for up to two years post-treatment. Some evidence suggests this preventive effect may extend beyond two years.

nodes.name: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a disease-modifying treatment for IgE-mediated allergic diseases.
nodes.content: AIT is recognized as a treatment that not only alleviates symptoms of IgE-mediated allergic diseases but also modifies the underlying disease process. It has both therapeutic effects during treatment and potential preventive effects beyond cessation of therapy.

nodes.name: A three-year course of AIT can prevent asthma in children with allergic rhinitis triggered by grass or birch pollen
nodes.content: A three-year course of subcutaneous or sublingual AIT is recommended for children and adolescents with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis caused by grass or birch pollen. This treatment can prevent asthma for up to two years post-AIT and has sustained effects on allergic rhinitis symptoms and medication use.

nodes.name: IgE水平与过敏严重程度相关
nodes.content: 研究表明，血清总IgE水平与过敏性疾病的严重程度呈正相关。在180例过敏性鼻炎患者中，重度患者的IgE中位数为256 IU/mL，显著高于轻度患者的89 IU/mL (p<0.001)。

nodes.name: 食物过敏患儿的年龄分布
nodes.content: 在0-2岁婴幼儿中，牛奶和鸡蛋是最常见的食物过敏原，占比分别为65%和55%。随着年龄增长，花生、坚果类过敏比例逐渐上升。

nodes.name: 证据：儿童过敏性鼻炎和哮喘患者应接受过敏原检测
nodes.content: 推荐专科医师对过敏性鼻炎或哮喘患儿做过敏原检测（强推荐）。

nodes.name: 证据：过敏原检测结果需结合临床表现解读
nodes.content: 推荐在临床表现的基础上解读检测结果。过敏原检测阳性时提示为致敏状态，但并不等同于罹患过敏性疾病（强推荐）。

nodes.name: 证据：不同过敏原检测方法适用于不同情况
nodes.content: 推荐基于不同过敏原检测特点与患儿具体疾病情况决定过敏原检测方式（强推荐）。

特应性皮炎的患病率趋势
nodes.content: 2020年全国流行病学调查显示，中国1-7岁儿童特应性皮炎患病率为12.94%，较2002年的3.07%显著上升。城市地区患病率(15.24%)高于农村地区(8.79%)。

nodes.name: 证据：儿童过敏性疾病发病率逐年上升
nodes.content: 儿童过敏性疾病发病率呈逐年上升趋势，罹患哮喘、过敏性鼻炎和湿疹等过敏性疾病不仅降低了儿童生活质量，而且增加家庭与社会的经济负担。

nodes.name: 证据：湿疹患儿不应常规进行过敏原检测
nodes.content: 不推荐对湿疹患儿常规做过敏原检测；推荐对持续中度至重度湿疹，常规治疗效果不佳的患儿做过敏原检测（强推荐）。

nodes.name: 免疫治疗的疗效评估
nodes.content: 一项包含1247例患者的多中心研究显示，标准化尘螨变应原免疫治疗3年后，症状评分较基线下降67%，药物使用减少72%，生活质量显著改善。

nodes.name: 尘螨是中国最常见的吸入性过敏原
nodes.content: 在中国不同地区的流行病学调查显示，户尘螨和粉尘螨是最主要的吸入性过敏原，阳性率可达60-80%。南方地区的尘螨过敏阳性率高于北方地区。

nodes.name: 证据：过敏原检测需规范化和标准化
nodes.content: 不同过敏原检测方法的适应证及其结果判断在儿科临床亟待规范。本共识以儿童过敏原检测相关的临床常见问题为导向，查阅相关文献，经多学科临床专家通过德尔菲投票方法达成共识，形成10个临床问题的推荐建议。

nodes.name: 证据：过敏原检测是儿童过敏性疾病管理的重要工具
nodes.content: 过敏原检测可以明确致敏变应原，为个体化管理过敏性疾病提供依据。常用的过敏原检测方法包括过敏原皮肤点刺试验和血清特异性IgE检测。

nodes.name: 证据：急性荨麻疹患儿不需常规过敏原检测
nodes.content: 不推荐对急性荨麻疹和慢性荨麻疹患儿常规进行过敏原检测（强推荐）。
